invalid.code: declare const source: Set<number>; const output = []; for (const value of source) { output.push(value); }
invalid.name: A8: for-of + push draining a Set into a fresh empty array - flagged

invalid.code: declare const source: Map<number, string>; const output = []; for (const entry of source) { output.push(entry); }
invalid.name: A8: for-of + push draining a Map into a fresh empty array - flagged

invalid.code: declare const source: Set<number>; const output = []; for (const value of source) { output['push'](value); }
invalid.name: computed string-literal key push() - flagged (CallIdentity resolves the signature, not the spelling)

invalid.code: declare const source: Set<number>; const PUSH = 'push' as const; const output = []; for (const value of source) { output[PUSH](value); }
invalid.name: const-held computed key push() - flagged

invalid.code: declare const sources: readonly Set<number>[]; sources.forEach((source) => { const output = []; for (const value of source) { output.push(value); } });
invalid.name: for-of + push nested inside a .forEach() callback - still flagged (detection is structural, not loop-gated)

invalid.code: function* ids() { yield 1; } const output = []; for (const value of ids()) { output.push(value); }
invalid.name: for-of + push draining a generator result - flagged

valid.code: declare const source: Set<number>; const output = Array.from(source);
valid.name: Array.from(iterable) itself - not flagged (retargeted: no longer the anti-pattern this rule targets, see A8 in the rule source)

valid.code: declare const source: Set<number>; const output = [...source];
valid.name: [...iterable] spread - not flagged (the recommended replacement, performance-neutral with Array.from)

valid.code: declare const source: number[]; const output = []; for (const value of source) { output.push(value); }
valid.name: for-of + push where the source is already an array - not flagged (copy/filter idiom, not the iterator-drain this rule targets)

valid.code: declare const source: Set<number>; const output = [1]; for (const value of source) { output.push(value); }
valid.name: for-of + push onto a non-empty pre-existing array - not flagged (Array.from/spread cannot reproduce this as a drop-in replacement)

valid.code: declare const source: Set<number>; let output; output = []; for (const value of source) { output.push(value); }
valid.name: accumulator declared without an initializer, assigned separately - not flagged (declaration statement is not `const x = [];`)

valid.code: declare const source: Set<number>; const output = []; for (const value of source) { output.push(value * 2); }
valid.name: pushed value is a transform of the loop binding, not the binding itself - not flagged (not equivalent to a bare Array.from/spread)

valid.code: declare const source: Set<number>; const output = []; for (const value of source) { console.log(value); output.push(value); }
valid.name: loop body has more than one statement - not flagged (not the pure single-statement drain shape)
